VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) – User Guide, Volume 1, Specifications
The VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) provides settlement functions for the BASE II System and
Single Message System (SMS), including Interlink. Clients and processors get settlement
information in a standardized set of reports using common business-oriented terminology. VSS
provides flexibility in defining financial relationships, selecting reports and report destinations,
Visa processes interchange transactions for SMS (including Interlink) and BASE II through
separate systems. SMS and BASE II perform their own clearing functions and VSS performs the
settlement functions for SMS and BASE II.
Clearing is the process of collecting an individual transaction from one client or
processor and delivering it to another.
Settlement is the process of calculating and determining the net financial position of
each client for all transactions that are cleared.
This figure shows the VSS clearing and settlement process.
VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) – User Guide, Volume 1, Specifications
Visa offers several settlement services options.
International Settlement Service – Used to settle all international transactions and
domestic transactions for clients that do not participate in a National Net Settlement
Service (NNSS) or Area Net Settlement Service (ANSS).
National Net Settlement Service (NNSS) – Allows clients within a country to settle
qualifying domestic transactions through a central settlement agent bank. Qualifying
transactions are those in which the merchant, acquirer, and issuer are in the same
country. Also, the transaction currency must be the local currency for that country for
Area Net Settlement Service (ANSS) – Allows clients within a defined area to settle
qualifying domestic transactions through a central settlement agent bank. Qualifying
transactions are those in which the merchant, acquirer, and issuer are in the same
defined area. Also, the transaction currency is the local currency for that defined area
Visa also offers intraday settlement for countries with an NNSS or ANSS. Intraday settlement
supports multiple settlement windows and facilitates delivery of settlement reports,
interchange clearing files, and funds transfer instructions multiple times a day.
VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) provides a variety of capabilities to clients.
Settlement relationships – VSS provides flexibility when defining settlement
relationships. Clients can define from two to eight levels of settlement relationships. The
different levels allow them to build and maintain the most appropriate settlement
relationships for their business needs. For example, the settlement relationship levels

Report layouts and formats – VSS reports provide a common layout for BASE II- and
SMS-cleared clients, allowing them to streamline their internal procedures. All VSS
reports are available in print-ready and machine-readable formats. VSS reports use
business-oriented terminology to better reflect the business needs of clients.
Report delivery options – Clients can have their reports sent to multiple locations,
including locations other than their processing centers. Interchange routing does not
determine the routing of settlement information.
Funds transfer points – The funds transfer point can be defined at any level in the
settlement structure. This flexibility allows clients using third-party processors to be
responsible for their own funds transfer.

These terms help define a lowest-level SRE:
Clearing Entity – The entity used by the clearing systems to determine processing rules.
In BASE II, a clearing entity is a 6-digit, Visa-assigned acquiring or issuing identifier or an
International Organization for Standardization (ISO)-assigned card range. In the Single
Message System (SMS), a clearing entity is the 6-digit, Visa-assigned acquiring or issuing

included in the definition of a lowest-level SRE.
Network – For Visa and VisaNet, the network is the telecommunications facility used for
message switching. For other card program networks (for example, Plus and Interlink),
the network dictates the product rules under which a transaction is processed.
Settlement Service – A settlement service directs transactions through either the Visa
International Settlement Service (the most commonly used settlement service) or
through a National Net Settlement Service (NNSS) or Area Net Settlement Service

transactions when the issuer, acquirer, and merchant are in the same location. Every
client must participate in the International Settlement Service and can also participate in
an NNSS or ANSS to which they qualify. The settlement service identifier is always
included as part of the definition of a lowest-level SRE. All SREs within a settlement
hierarchy must be for the same settlement service.

(VSS)–900) and Summary Reconciliation Report (VSS–900–S) match the COUNT and CLEARING AMOUNT totals for each business

For BASE II-connected clients that participate in the Custom Payment Service (CPS) and Chargeback Reduction Service (CRS),
disposition of exception transactions is shown separately on the VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) reconciliation reports.
Transactions submitted during the processing day and held over for CRS validation are reported on the VSS reconciliation reports:
Total counts and amounts submitted and held over are under TO CRS.
Total counts and amounts of financial transactions held over from a previous day and that successfully passed CRS validation
are reported. Total counts and amounts are reported under FROM CRS ACCEPTED. The number and value are under TOTAL
Total counts and amounts of financial transactions that are held over and that failed CRS validation are reported. Counts and
amounts are shown under FROM CRS RETURNED.
Total counts and amounts of financial transactions that were sent to CRS in the previous cycle but are not being settled in the
current cycle (because currency rates are unavailable) are shown under FROM CRS ACCEPTED TO WAREHOUSE.
The counts for nonfinancial transactions are shown in the NON-FINANCIAL TRANSACTIONS sections of the VSS reconciliation
reports. These counts for transactions sent to and from CRS are totaled under TOTAL SENT TO and RECEIVED FROM VISA.
There is a total count under TOTAL NON-FINANCIAL.
This subsection applies only to clients in countries using CPS that have a processing delay for exception items.

VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) hierarchy implementation can be done using a standard or a
custom method. Clients must determine which implementation strategy to use.
Standard – This implementation type creates a two-level hierarchy, with one top
settlement reporting entity (SRE) that includes parameters that define the entire
hierarchy, such as the settlement currency code. The top SRE also represents a
summary of all SREs below the top SRE. In a standard hierarchy, the top SRE represents
all activity cleared (processed) by the processor. The lowest-level SREs are either
identifiers (acquirers and issuers) or account ranges (issuers). Funds transfer can occur
at the top level or at the lowest level (client-level settlement).
Reporting options for a standard hierarchy can be defined by groups of acquiring or
issuing identifiers or can apply to all SREs within the hierarchy. Multiple report delivery
destinations must be requested as a custom implementation.
